newsitem.title: USA: AWAY ON BUSINESS: Travelers do the ticketing.
newsitem.headline: AWAY ON BUSINESS: Travelers do the ticketing.

text.p: Technology may be carrying the business traveller into a do-it-yourself era when it comes to booking airline, hotel and other trip arrangements.
The result could be time savings for travelers who now have to go through a corporate travel manager or private travel agency, and more control and choice over what happens.

John Ackermann, president and chief executive officer of E-Travel Inc. in Concord, Mass., estimates that from 20 percent to 30 percent of business trips may be booked through electronic sytems, such as the one his company recently launched, in the next five years.

The system, called E-Travel, allows a company to keep control over the travel policies it sets -- which airlines are used, what fares are preferred and so on -- but lets the individual traveller make the arrangements from the desktop or even on the road from a laptop, within those policy confines.

"It actually presents a number of options that would normally be overlooked in dealing with an agent over the telephone," where there is pressure to get the transaction finished as fast as possible, Ackermann said.

Among other things, those booking an airline flight have access to cabin seating charts showing which seats are sold and where there may be a preferred spot such as on the aisle or in a row with an empty middle seat.
Transactions are done through an Internet dial-up to the E-Travel site, but the software is customised for each company to reflect preferences and expense parameters.

Much of business travel involves trips to the same city or location -- by one estimate 70 percent of it -- so making travel arrangements need not be time consuming if the basic information is in a system.
Ackermann said one major Boston-based mutual fund company is now using E-Travel and one of the 10 largest U.S. travel agencies, Travel One, is using it for corporate clients.
He said the company has a European arm, E-Travel Europe AB, based in Stockholm, which plans to enter that market soon.

The programme is affilated with Worldspan, the airline computer reservation system operated by Delta, Trans World Airlines, Northwest and other carriers. Through it links to all major airlines are available.
